societies.name: Tacoma — Orbital human oversight requirements
societies.society: The legally retained human station-crew cohort under the Human Oversight Accord

scope.period: The established employment regime before Venturis’s staged accident
scope.population: Tacoma’s six employed human crew members as a narrow legal-labor cohort
exclusions: The entire Earth population as six workers

societies.description:
The Human Oversight Accord prevents Venturis from deploying its fully automated orbital holiday-home project. Human staffing therefore persists despite available capacity for uncrewed operation, supporting a zero-variant comparison. The record is deliberately limited to the legally retained station-crew cohort rather than claiming that all Earth employment is make-work. These people still perform useful medical, technical, administrative and other tasks; a legal reason to retain humans does not make every action pointless.

Authority lies with the company, which consults a strategic AI but also directs the station system. That supports concentrated control with uncertainty about the AI’s effective influence. The employer’s deliberate attempt to sacrifice its crew makes their material security weak even though ordinary station life provides support. Rescue by outsiders does not establish an enforceable company guarantee. All six scoped residents are employed crew performing real work, so their nonworking estimate is zero with a small uncertainty allowance. This narrow result is not a population-wide unemployment statistic, and neither cryosleep nor unbuilt vacation homes enlarges the cohort.

guarantees.basis: Company-supplied support can be deliberately withdrawn in a plan to kill the crew; external rescue does not create an employer entitlement.

control.basis: Corporate leadership and strategic AI act together, but company orders retain a clear role; their exact balance is uncertain.

nonworking.basis: The denominator is explicitly the six employed crew, who perform useful tasks; this is not the wider human population.

evidence.claim: Law retains human oversight despite planned full automation, and the company seeks repeal through a staged fatal incident.
evidence.locator: Plot: Human Oversight Accord and Venturis/JUNO scheme

uncertainties: Narrow six-person employment cohort, not a whole-world work census.
Real useful work persists; not every task is proven unnecessary.
The legal barrier is established; its complete legislative purpose is not reconstructed.
Corporate/AI agency is a broad uncertain estimate.

review.method: Second pass against the gathered passages, including explicit uncertainty; no independent reviewer

review_notes: Previous goal turn was substantive progress: 556 processed / 122 retained to 628 / 133. This continuation resumes authoritative state rather than the stale objective checkpoint.
Twelve fast dispositions and one narrow zero-variant record. No full game transcript, novel, ARG decoding or source download.
Tacoma’s legal oversight cohort is not an entire world. Corporate AI advice is not automatically sovereign AI control, and useful crew work still counts.
Citizen Sleeper’s official description confirms actual paid survival work. Stray’s artificial successors and one human-derived drone are not identical populations.
Unrelated real-world Tacoma job listings, speculative forum answers and player wishes were discarded. Official descriptions replaced weak lore when available.
